key_insight: Standard DBSCAN restricts the trackable velocity range in event-based particle tracking; recursive clustering with multiple temporal normalizations is proposed to address this limitation.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets 2D, two-component particle tracking across varying flow speeds without assuming a characteristic time scale or typical velocity.
method: Diagnose DBSCAN’s velocity-range limitation using a synthetic two-particle system.
Apply DBSCAN recursively with multiple temporal normalizations.
Retain only clusters that satisfy validation criteria.
evidence_signal: Evaluation uses realistic synthetic datasets from turbulent-flow simulations, parameter studies, event-cluster tracking metrics, and an application to experimental turbulent-flow data.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative accuracy or velocity-range gains, so practical benefits and parameter sensitivity require checking the full paper.
paper_title: On the velocity range limitation of DBSCAN for event-based particle tracking and a proposed solution
